Note::TexAccessor::display_math¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::display_math() const

Extract Block-Math Fragments¶

display_math() finds display-style math fragments in every Text cell. It recognizes the two source forms that delimit an anonymous display directly: $$...$$ and \[...\]. The returned token includes both delimiters, so it can be inspected, transformed, or emitted again without guessing which spelling the source used.

This is extraction, not conversion. Inline $...$ and \(...\) fragments are ignored, prose remains outside the result, and the receiver is unchanged. Use math_blocks() when inline and display math belong in the same result, or inline_math() when only inline fragments are wanted.

Scanning is lane-local and source ordered. Each input cell contributes zero or more tokens to a flat Text Note; the Int64 offsets() Note records where each cell’s range begins and ends. Consequently, a rank-two receiver still produces a flat token Note, but its four logical cells produce five offsets. Empty cells and cells without display math contribute repeated boundaries rather than placeholder strings.

Only complete delimiter pairs are returned. An unmatched opener or closer does not create a partial token. The operation does not parse commands inside a fragment or validate mathematical syntax. Undefined input produces an undefined token Note with offsets [0]; non-text input is rejected. Work is linear in the bytes scanned plus the bytes copied into matching tokens.

Example 1: Distinguish Display And Inline Math¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(inline $a$ then $$b+c$$ and \[d=e\])",
    R"($$first$$ between $$second$$)",
    R"(plain text and \(inline\))"});
const auto blocks = source.tex().display_math();

std::cout << blocks.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["$$b+c$$", "\\[d=e\\]", "$$first$$", "$$second$$"]

The inline fragments do not appear. Both display spellings retain their original delimiters.

Example 2: Recover Cell Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = blocks.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 4, 4]

Cell zero owns tokens [0, 2), cell one owns [2, 4), and cell two owns the empty range [4, 4).

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Dtypes¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().display_math();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().display_math();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "display math Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
display math Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • inline_math: extract only inline math fragments.

  • math_blocks: extract both inline and display math.

  • add_math_delimiters: wrap whole cells instead of extracting fragments.
